question: Where does hipEngine Gemma 4 stand against the latest llama.cpp on the same W7900, for plain prefill and decode and for MTP?
model: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_XL (/mnt/nvme1/models/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf, 17010980576 bytes); MTP head mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q8_0.gguf

previous_comparator.note: 506 commits later, not faster on this model and device

commands.llamacpp: scripts/gemma4_llamacpp_reference_bench.py --pci 0000:0d:00.0 --server <45451c3 llama-server> --source <tree> --prompt P --output 128 --context P+256 --samples 3 --warmup 1 (server: -ngl 99 -fa on -ctk bf16 -ctv bf16 -np 1 -b 4096 -ub 1024 --no-cache-prompt --fit off)

plain_ladder.pairing: each prompt length ran llama.cpp then hipEngine back to back; prompt ids byte-identical (sha256 equal at every length)
plain_ladder.ids_note: first-sample generated ids equal at every length through 65536; at 131072 the two engines' greedy outputs differ

mtp.prompts: benchmarks/prompts/mtpbench-code-general-ja.jsonl + benchmarks/prompts/gdn-prefill-category-heldouts.jsonl, 18 prompts x 2 samples, chat template rendered by hipEngine and sent to llama.cpp as the same token ids
mtp.timing_scope: whole request wall time including the short prefill, 128 tokens, EOS honored (no row stopped early)
mtp.llamacpp_server: -md <head> --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 -ngld 99 -ctkd bf16 -ctvd bf16, otherwise the plain-ladder flags with -c 1024; /completion with the prompt as token ids, cache_prompt false

llamacpp.note: --spec-draft-sampling probabilistic (added in 1fb7ef3) is slower than plain decoding here; greedy draft is the default

hipengine_production.draft_law: drawn from the head's distribution, exact speculative sampling

verify_block_ms.method: llama-bench -p R -n 0 -d 600 -r 10 -fa 1 -ctk bf16 -ctv bf16 (prompt processing of R rows at depth 600) against hipEngine Gemma4Runner.forward(R rows, verification=True) after a 600-token prompt, production

limitations: The MTP comparison uses one prompt family pair (18 prompts).
llama.cpp verify-block times come from llama-bench prompt processing, which includes no draft step.
